claims.text: What the strip looks like A rate over 100 w ± three diff P-wave shapes; often in COPD.
claims.quote: Rate > 100 At least 3 distinct P-wave morphologies Often in COPD patients

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Rate: > 100 (USU 100–150; up to 250)
claims.quote: Heart rate > 100 bpm (usually 100-150 bpm; may be as high as 250 bpm).

claims.text: Rhythm: irregularly irreg, w varying PP, PR and RR intervals
claims.quote: Irregularly irregular rhythm with varying PP, PR and RR intervals.

claims.text: P waves: ± 3 distinct morphologies in the same lead
claims.quote: At least 3 distinct P-wave morphologies in the same lead.

claims.text: Baseline: isoelectric b/n P waves (⍉flutter waves)
claims.quote: Isoelectric baseline between P-waves (i.e. no flutter waves).
Absence of a single dominant atrial pacemaker (i.e. not just sinus rhythm with frequent PACs).

claims.text: Conduction: some P waves may ⍉conduct; others may conduct aberrantly
claims.quote: Some P waves may be nonconducted; others may be aberrantly conducted to the ventricles.

claims.text: vs AF: the presence of P waves distinguishes MAT from AF
claims.quote: The presence of P waves distinguishes multifocal atrial tachycardia from atrial fibrillation.

claims.text: Wandering atrial pacemaker: the same irregularly irreg multifocal rhythm @ a rate ≤ 100
claims.quote: Wandering atrial pacemaker (multifocal atrial rhythm) is an irregularly irregular rhythm caused by the random discharge of multiple ectopic atrial foci. By definition, heart rate is ≤ 100 beats/minute.

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) Mech: ↑atrial automaticity from Rt atrial dilate (cor pulmonale), ↑sympathetic drive, hypoxia and hypercarbia, beta-agonists, theophylline, hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia (ex, from diuretics or beta-agonists)
claims.quote: Right atrial dilatation (from cor pulmonale) Increased sympathetic drive Hypoxia and hypercarbia Beta-agonists Theophylline Electrolyte abnormalities: Hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia (e.g. secondary to diuretics / beta-agonists) The net result is increased atrial automaticity.

claims.text: Most commonly severe COPD or CHF
claims.quote: Most commonly seen in patients with severe COPD or congestive heart failure.

claims.text: USU seriously ill elderly pts w resp failure (ex, COPD or CHF exacerbation)
claims.quote: Usually occurs in seriously ill elderly patients with respiratory failure (e.g. exacerbation of COPD / CHF).

claims.text: Typically a transitional rhythm b/n freq PACs and A-flutter or AF
claims.quote: It is typically a transitional rhythm between frequent premature atrial complexes (PACs) and atrial flutter / fibrillation.

claims.text: A poor prognostic sign during acute illness — death comes from the underlying illness, ⍉the arrhythmia
claims.quote: The development of MAT during an acute illness is a poor prognostic sign, associated with a 60% in-hospital mortality and mean survival of just over a year. Death occurs due to the underlying illness; not the arrhythmia itself.

claims.text: Sx When present, those of rapid tachy
claims.quote: Symptoms, when they occur, are those of rapid tachycardia.

claims.text: Tx Tx the underlying dx — MAT tends to resolve w it
claims.quote: Tends to resolve following treatment of the underlying disorder.

claims.text: If arrhythmia-directed therapy = needed: IV magnesium, IV verapamil or a BB; digoxin, class I or III antiarrhythmics and cardioversion USU don't work
claims.quote: When therapy directed at the arrhythmia is required, the most effective agents are IV magnesium, IV verapamil, and a beta-blocker (5). Treatment with digoxin, class I or III antiarrhythmic medications, or cardioversion is usually ineffective
